title: City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment
ballot_label: City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment
summary: King City asks voters to amend and restate its city charter, last revised in 2006, following a Charter Review Committee process. The City's explanatory statement says it keeps the council-manager form, number of councilors and mayor-selection method, and revises provisions on vacancies, councilor duties and compensation. Your Oregon News reports it would also allow an urban renewal agency and remove the 2012 voter-approval requirement for rail transit spending. If rejected, the current charter remains.
yes_means: A yes vote adopts the City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment, changing the city charter.
no_means: A no vote leaves the current King City charter in effect without the proposed amendment.

arguments.author: Howard Suesserman, candidate for King City Council
arguments.statement: In his voters' pamphlet candidate statement, King City Council candidate Howard Suesserman says Measure 34-354 would update the city charter but does not let citizens directly elect their mayor.
arguments.excerpt: The November ballot includes Measure 34-354 to update the city charter, but it fails to let citizens directly elect their mayor.

source.publisher: Washington County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. WC-19)

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed on WC-19 in Howard Suesserman's candidate statement; he is a King City Council candidate. This is a candidate statement, not a filed measure argument; the gap says so.

gaps: No YES arguments collected: the county voters' pamphlet measure pages (WC-57 to WC-58) could not be read, and no attributed supporting statement was found; Your Oregon News (Sept 28, 2026) reports council approval but quotes no one.
NO side has only one item, from a candidate statement rather than a filed measure argument; filed pamphlet arguments, if any, could not be read.
Ballot question, summary and explanatory statement not collected: the county ballot-title PDF is a scanned image and the city's charter page links only the current charter.

ballot_label_verification.note: Caption matches county document title; scanned PDF.

summary_verification.note: The collector's gap says no explanatory statement was found, but the City's measure page (https://www.ci.king-city.or.us/government/city_recorder/city_of_king_city_charter_modernization_amendments.php) links an official EXPLANATORY STATEMENT PDF (https://cms6.revize.com/revize/kingcityornew/document_center/Government/Elections/2026/Charter/EXPLANATORY%20STATEMENT.pdf). The summary is rebased on that official text. The press-only points (urban renewal, rail provision) are kept and attributed to Your Oregon News (Ray Pitz, 2026-09-28, https://youroregonnews.com/2026/09/28/king-city-to-ask-for-charter-amendments-on-filling-vacancies-possible-council-compensation/). The YON points were confirmed on that page.

no_means_verification.note: Confirmed: the explanatory statement says the current Charter remains in effect if the measure fails.

verification_summary.balance_notes: 0 YES / 1 NO; the YES gap is documented. The NO item is a voters' pamphlet candidate statement (T1), not a filed measure argument; there are 0 explanatory-text items and 0 press items. The pamphlet gives the measure 2 pages (WC-57 to WC-58), which may include filed arguments (unverified). The official explanatory statement on the City site was missed. It is neutral and could supply explainer items for both sides in a re-collection. The spot search found no attributed supporter or opponent quotes.
